findings.title: Migration crashes when the embed_category site setting has no DB row
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. Site settings only have a row in the `site_settings` table when an admin has overridden the default; on any install where `embed_category` was never changed from its empty default (or was set to a blank/non-matching value so the join returns nothing), the result set is empty, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking the deploy. The result needs a nil check before indexing (the same pattern is repeated on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`).

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw, keeping scheme/path that lookups will never match
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting explicitly supported values like `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (the old specs set exactly those values). The new `EmbeddableHost` model strips the scheme and path in a `before_validation` callback, but the migration inserts the old values with raw SQL, bypassing the model entirely. After migration, rows contain e.g. `https://example.com/1234`, while `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `uri.host` (`example.com`) against the stored value, so every previously configured host that included a scheme or path silently stops being allowed — existing embedded comment installs break until an admin manually re-saves each host.

findings.title: Migration interpolates setting values directly into SQL without escaping
findings.body: The migration builds INSERT statements with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. `h` comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which was free text; a host entry containing a single quote will produce invalid SQL and fail the migration mid-way (and in principle allows SQL injection). Use `sanitize`/`quote` or a bound parameter instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: record_for_host does not downcase the incoming host and cannot match hosts saved with a port
findings.body: `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` where `host` is `uri.host`. Ruby's URI parser preserves the case of the host (it is only downcased by `#normalize`), so a referer like `http://EVILTROUT.COM/page` will not match the stored lowercase `eviltrout.com` — the comparison should be against `host.downcase`. Additionally, the host validation regex on line 2 permits an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), so an admin can save `example.com:3000`, but `uri.host` strips the port, meaning such a record can never match and embedding from that host is always rejected. Either reject ports in validation or include the port in the lookup.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If an `EmbeddableHost` is built without a host (e.g. the admin controller receives a request missing `embeddable_host[host]`, or code does `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return unless self.host` (or `self.host = self.host.to_s`) and add a presence validation.

findings.title: update and destroy raise NoMethodError for an unknown host id instead of 404
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then use the result without a nil check: `update` passes nil into `save_host`, where `host.host = ...` raises NoMethodError, and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil. A request for a deleted or bogus id returns a 500. Both actions should raise `Discourse::NotFound` (or use `find`) when the record is missing.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint or validation on host
findings.body: Neither the model nor the migration enforces uniqueness of `host`, so admins can create duplicate rows for the same host pointing at different categories. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then uses `.first`, making the category chosen for imported embedded topics arbitrary, and the admin UI shows conflicting duplicate rows. Add a unique index plus `validates_uniqueness_of :host, case_sensitive: false`.

findings.title: Contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines all the category fabricators (`category`, `diff_category`, `happy_category`, `private_category`). The Fabrication gem loads every file in the directory so the test suite still runs, but the file names no longer match their contents — the new file's content belongs in `category_fabricator.rb` and vice versa.

findings.title: Plural *_ids hydration produces arrays of undefined and deletes the raw ids even when nothing was resolved
findings.body: In `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch maps `foo_ids` through `_lookupSubType` and then unconditionally sets `obj[plural] = hydrated` and deletes `obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which only assigns and deletes when a hydrated object was actually found), this branch assigns even when `_lookupSubType` returned undefined for some or all ids — producing e.g. `colors: [undefined, undefined]` and destroying the original `color_ids` data. Any payload containing a plural id array whose collection is missing from the root (or partially missing ids) is silently corrupted. It should skip the assignment when nothing resolved, and ideally compact/filter unresolved ids; the `|| []` on the map result is also dead code since `map` always returns an array.

findings.title: New admin endpoints have no request specs
findings.body: The specs added for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (and `Admin::EmbeddingController`) only assert the class is a subclass of AdminController. There is no coverage for create/update/destroy behavior — authorization (non-staff rejected), the default-to-uncategorized category fallback, validation error rendering, deleting a host, or the embedding show endpoint. These endpoints implement the core of the feature (including the nil-record crashes noted above) and currently have zero functional coverage.
